sentences.text:
Order
Order No. 20.02.2023  I.A. No.747 of 2022  04.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/ physical mode).
This is an application for bail.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

The petitioner has been convicted for the offences under sections 376(2)(l)/450/506 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/-
(rupees five thousand), in default, to undergo further R.I. for a period of six months for the offence under section 376(2)(l) of the Indian Penal Code, to undergo R.I. for seven years // 2 // and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/- (rupees two thousand), in default, to undergo further R.I. for three months for the offence under section 450 of the Indian Penal Code and to undergo R.I. for two years for the offence under section 506 of the Indian Penal Code and all the sentences were directed to run concurrently by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge, Chatrapur in S.T. Case No.41 of 2017.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 19.09.2016 and he was released from judicial custody on 17.08.2018 and then, he was again taken into judicial custody on 17.07.2021 and since then he is in judicial custody.

He further submits that the victim is a major and the F.I.R. was lodged thirteen days after the alleged occurrence and the medical evidence does not corroborate the victim's evidence and there are good chances of success in appeal and balance of convenience is his favour and therefore, the bail application of the petitioner may be favourably considered.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and placed the evidence of P.W.2 and P.W.5.

Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner, nature of evidence adduced by the prosecution during trial, delay in lodging of F.I.R., absence of any chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future and balance of convenience // 3 // being in his favour and further taking into account the period of detention of the petitioner in judicial custody, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
Let the petitioner be released on bail pending disposal of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court on such other conditions as the learned trial Court may deem just and proper The I.A. is accordingly disposed of.
(S.K. Sahoo) Judge 05. Heard.

There shall be stay of realization of fine amount imposed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge,
Chatrapur in S.T. Case No.41 of 2017 till disposal of the criminal appeal.
Issue certified copy as per rules.

(S.K. Sahoo) Judge Sipun Rajendra Sahu vs State Of Odisha on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93347700/
